text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today to $142.79, recouping losses from earlier in the week as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East drove oil prices higher. Iran's escalation of threats against U.S. forces and the arrival of a third American carrier in the Persian Gulf stoked concerns about potential disruptions to global oil supply, with Brent crude (world oil price) climbing to $92.14 per barrel. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly improve profit margins on barrels they sell.

The stock had dipped to $140.52 just yesterday before today's rebound, suggesting the market was pricing in the geopolitical risk as news broke. Heating oil prices have also surged 59% year-over-year, signaling broader energy market tightness heading into winter—a backdrop that tends to support higher crude valuations and benefit producers.
